quiz.title: Module 1 — Tuesday — Introduction to Personal Branding
quiz.description: Tuesday's quiz covers what personal branding actually is, what it is not, finding clarity about yourself before creating content, identifying a target audience, choosing content directions by pathway, and why consistency and starting before you feel ready both matter.

questions.prompt: What is personal branding primarily about?
options: Getting as many followers as possible
Intentionally presenting yourself and what you want people to associate with you
Creating a perfect image that hides your weaknesses
Posting every day to increase engagement
questions.explanation: Personal branding is the intentional presentation of yourself and what people come to associate with you — not a follower count.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT presented as a fundamental part of developing a personal brand?
options: Your interests and skills
Your experiences and perspective
Pretending to be someone you're not
The way you consistently communicate
questions.explanation: Pretending to be someone you're not is explicitly ruled out. A brand grows from your real identity, interests, skills and perspective.

questions.prompt: Before creating content for a personal brand, which question would be most useful to ask yourself?
options: How can I become famous as quickly as possible?
What am I interested in, and what do I want people to associate with me?
How can I copy the most successful creator in my niche?
How many followers should I gain this week?
questions.explanation: Clarity about your interests and what you want to be associated with is the starting point the lesson asks for.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of identifying a target audience?
options: To make sure only one type of person can see your content
To understand who your content is intended to reach and what they may care about
To guarantee that every person who sees your content will follow you
To prevent your personal brand from evolving
questions.explanation: Knowing your audience helps you understand who the content is for and what matters to them — it does not narrow who may see it.

questions.prompt: A Video Editing student wants to build a personal brand. Which content direction would best align with the module?
options: Posting unrelated viral memes exclusively
Only posting motivational quotes
Showcasing edits, documenting progress, sharing editing insights, and showing the creative process
Waiting until they become a professional editor before posting anything
questions.explanation: The module lists exactly this for Video Editing — edits, progress, insights and process — over waiting until you feel qualified.

questions.prompt: Why is consistency important when building a personal brand?
options: It guarantees that every post will go viral
It allows people to repeatedly see and associate you with your work, ideas, or area of interest over time
It means you should never experiment with your content
It eliminates the need to understand your audience
questions.explanation: A brand is built through repeated exposure — consistency is what lets people recognise you and what you stand for.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes how a personal brand develops?
options: It is created completely before you publish your first piece of content
It develops through learning, experimenting, creating, and discovering more about yourself over time
It depends primarily on having a large number of followers
It requires you to choose one topic and never change it
questions.explanation: The lesson is clear that your brand evolves as you learn, experiment and discover more about yourself.

questions.prompt: A student says, "I don't know exactly what my personal brand should become, so I'll wait until I have everything figured out before I start posting." Based on the lesson, what is the best response?
options: That's correct; clarity must come before any content creation
They should focus on gaining followers first
They should start with a direction, create, learn, and improve as their brand becomes clearer
They should copy an established creator until they understand branding
questions.explanation: The lesson's whole stance is that you learn by creating. Start with a direction and let clarity arrive through the process.
